items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: And so he got the three of us together and he showed us a little chord and everything.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Did anybody in your family play instruments? I mean, where did you get the idea you wanted to play an instrument?
Well, my father was a musician. He played guitar and played viola, played a little bass. What was his name? George Sayle.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: So then he taught me, I remember, after he taught me how to play three changes, I remember in the key of G.

ctx.x: It was different from what now?

From listening to brass bands in Donovanville, you know. Oh, I see. Because they were strictly readers, you know. But Claiborne Williams did have an orchestra band, but I mean, by me being a kid, I didn't really get a chance to go out there then, you see. Yeah. Yeah. So we... She lived up there on Birdhead and Oak. Like I said, all the bands used to stop there. And I don't know, I forgot the time behind there. We moved on Ramport Street between 6th and Washington. And I went to a school called the Holy Ghost…
seemed like he had this all playing out, what he wanted me to play.
